name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans R+15, one of the most Republican seats in Arizona
Gosar's incumbency and roughly 12-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage
No public polling; Polymarket prices Democratic win odds near 4%
Sterbinsky raised modestly but has little cash left after the primary
model.rationale: Gosar benefits from a fifteen-point Republican district lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge, while Sterbinsky enters the general with minimal resources after primary spending. With no polls available and markets pricing Democratic odds around four percent, the seat stays in Republican hands even in a year when national conditions favor Democrats.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Gosar below majority support or significant outside spending against him would be the clearest sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 9th District leans heavily Republican, and Paul Gosar returns as the incumbent with the advantages that status brings. He has raised about $580,000 and holds roughly $303,000 on hand, while Democrat Dani Sterbinsky raised about $354,000 but enters the general election with only around $26,000 in cash after primary spending. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

Public polling of the contest is absent, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4 percent chance of winning. The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, combined with Gosar's incumbency and financial edge, makes him a clear favorite. Sterbinsky's fundraising shows some Democratic engagement in the seat, but the resource gap and the district's fundamentals point to a Republican hold, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
